To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AP3B2 is a novel gene for EOEE, that the AP-3 adaptor complex is a key component in the pathogenesis of EOEE, and that the AP-1 and AP-3 adaptor complexes are both involved in the pathogenesis and the phenotypic spectrum of the disease.
we identified autosomal-recessive variations in the AP3B2 gene in a homogeneous group of patients with EOEE.
AP3B2 mutations cause a new autosomal-recessive disorder characterized by early onset epilepsy, optic atrophy, developmental delay, and postnatal brain atrophy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of a novel epileptic encephalyopathy, EOEE with optic atrophy.
the first description of AP3B-related epileptic encephaly.
a novel form of EOEE associated with optic atrophy and developmental impairment caused by mutations in AP3 complex subunits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

autosomal-recessive variations in AP3B1 cause Hermansky–Pudlak syndrome type II, autosomal-recessive AP3D1 mutations cause the severe disorder described in this paper, and autosomal-recessivemutations in AP3B 2 cause an EOEE with optic atrophy.
autosomal-recessive defects of the AP- 3 complex cause a severe epileptic encephalo-myopathy with variable clinical features, depending on the isoform of the AP-2 complex involved.
the AP-3 adaptor complex is a key player in neurodevelopment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AP-3 adaptor protein complex is essential for neuronal development.
the AP-3 adaptor complex is crucial for the biogenesis of synaptic vesicles and lysosomes.
the AP-3 subunits are crucial for neuronal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AP3B2 is a novel gene for EOEE.
mutations in AP3 complex components can cause a wide spectrum of phenotypic presentations, from the severe to the mild.
the AP-3 subunit mutations cause a continuum of phenotypes, from mild to severe.
